```{r setup}
source("R/_load_all.R")
library(ggplot2)
A <- readRDS("results/app_data.rds")
P <- A$p
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
pal <- c("#2a6f97", "#e07a5f", "#3d405b", "#81b29a", "#f2cc8f")
s <- A$settings
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Iteration cap
At the project's request, every iteration count is capped at **`r s$iter_cap`**:
the base sample size *n*, the bootstrap replicates *R*, and the number of random
facilities. Cushway et al. (2026) grew *n* until every confidence interval was
narrower than 0.05, which took *n* ≥ 60,000. At *n* = `r s$n` the intervals are much
wider, so read "non-influential" as **"not shown to be influential at this sample
size"**.
:::

# 1. Data

`r nrow(P)` asset groups × `r ncol(P)` ratings. A to F- are condition grades and CF is
the conditional failure probability, the worst case.

```{r checks}
knitr::kable(A$checks)
```

```{r curves, fig.height=6}
d <- A$long
ggplot(d[!d$is_cf, ], aes(rating, p_fail, group = asset_group)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5, colour = pal[1]) +
  geom_point(data = d[d$is_cf, ], shape = 5, colour = pal[2]) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 0.01)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Annual P(fail), log scale",
       title = "All 31 curves (diamonds = CF worst case)")
```

On the logit scale the steps between neighbouring grades shrink steadily from A
to C. There is a smaller drop at C → C- and a **large jump at D- → F+**:

```{r steps}
L <- qlogis(P[, A$grades])
lab <- paste(head(A$grades, -1), "→", A$grades[-1])
D <- t(apply(L, 1, diff))                       # groups x 13 steps
steps <- data.frame(step = factor(rep(lab, each = nrow(D)), levels = lab),
                    value = as.vector(D))
ggplot(steps, aes(step, value)) + geom_boxplot(fill = pal[1], alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "logit step") + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

# 2. Curve shape

A piecewise model with three segments, `logit(p) = a_s + b_s·log(g + c)`, matches
every group closely. The median logit RMSE is `r signif(median(A$fits$summary$rmse_logit), 2)`
and the worst relative error is `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * max(A$fits$summary$max_rel_err))`.
The fit is descriptive only. The sensitivity analyses perturb the table directly.

```{r fits}
f <- A$fits$summary
knitr::kable(head(f[order(-f$max_rel_err), c("asset_group", "offset", "rmse_logit", "max_rel_err")], 5),
             digits = 4, caption = "Five worst-fitting groups")
```

# 3. One notch of grade error

```{r notch, fig.height=6}
e <- A$elasticity
ggplot(e, aes(grade, asset_group, fill = pct_per_notch)) + geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "B", direction = -1, name = "% per notch") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "% change in annual P(fail) per notch of grade")
```

One notch matters most at the best grades and **around D-/F+**. From A, A- or B+,
moving one notch worse raises P(fail) by 31% to 243%. Across C- to D-, one notch
is worth only about 10% to 38%. At the D- → F+ boundary, a one-notch error changes P(fail)
by `r sprintf("%.0f%% to %.0f%%", min(100*(e$worse_notch_ratio[e$grade=="D-"]-1)), max(100*(e$worse_notch_ratio[e$grade=="D-"]-1)))`.

# 4. Misclassification

With a 60/20/20 misclassification matrix (60% correct, 20% for each neighbouring
notch), the expected P(fail) is **higher** than the table value at most grades,
because the curves are convex:

```{r mc, fig.height=6}
mc <- misclass_effect(P, misclass_matrix(0.6, 1))
ggplot(mc, aes(grade, asset_group, fill = bias_ratio)) + geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = 1, low = pal[1], high = pal[2], name = "Expected ÷\ntable") +
  labs(x = "Observed grade", y = NULL)
```

# 5. Multi-year risk

Cumulative risk over *T* years is `1 − Π(1 − pₜ)`. When the grade can worsen over
time (Markov deterioration with annual probability *q*), multi-year risk rises
much faster than the constant-grade figure:

```{r multiyear}
my <- A$multiyear
ex <- my[my$asset_group %in% c("Electrical A", "Concrete A", "Earthen A") & my$start_grade == "C", ]
ggplot(ex, aes(year, cumulative, colour = scenario)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~asset_group) + scale_colour_manual(values = pal[1:3]) +
  labs(y = "P(failed by year t)", x = "Year", colour = NULL,
       title = "Starting at grade C") + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# 6. Global sensitivity: single asset (L2)

The inputs are the grade (±1 notch) and the curve level, slope and F-jump (each
±20%). The 10-year runs add the deterioration rate *q* ~ U(0, 0.3).

```{r l2}
i <- A$l2_influence
agg <- aggregate(cbind(Ti, influential) ~ parameter + horizon, i, mean)
agg$horizon <- ifelse(agg$horizon == 1, "Annual", "10-year")
names(agg) <- c("Input", "Output", "Mean Tᵢ", "Share flagged influential")
knitr::kable(agg, digits = 3)
```

```{r l2plot, fig.height=4}
i$segment <- grade_segment(i$grade_index)
ggplot(i[i$horizon == 1, ], aes(grade, Ti, colour = parameter, group = parameter)) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "line", linewidth = 1) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = function(y) data.frame(y = median(y), ymin = quantile(y, 0.1), ymax = quantile(y, 0.9)),
               geom = "ribbon", alpha = 0.1, aes(fill = parameter), colour = NA) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) + scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(x = "Observed grade", y = "Total-order Tᵢ (median and 10th–90th percentile over groups)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

**Findings:**

- The **grade** dominates at A to C, where the steps between grades are large.
- **Curve slope** dominates across C- to D-, because the slope multiplier scales
  the whole distance from grade A, which is large by then.
- The **F-jump** only matters at F+ to F-.
- The **level** (±20% odds) is a small contributor everywhere.
- In 10-year runs, **deterioration rate** takes a noticeable share
  (mean Tᵢ ≈ `r sprintf("%.2f", agg[agg$Input=="q","Mean Tᵢ"])`).

```{r seg}
knitr::kable(A$segment_tests, digits = 3,
             caption = "Kruskal–Wallis: does Tᵢ differ by grade segment? (median Tᵢ per segment)")
```

# 7. Facility structures (L3)

```{r ens, fig.height=4.5}
en <- A$ensemble
en$horizon <- ifelse(en$horizon == 1, "Annual", "10-year")
ggplot(en, aes(structure, pct_noninfluential, fill = structure)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA) + geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~horizon) + scale_fill_manual(values = pal, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% inputs non-influential",
       title = sprintf("%d random facilities", s$n_facilities))
```

```{r ens_tests}
knitr::kable(A$structure_tests, digits = 3, caption = "Friedman tests (facility = block)")
```

As in the paper, the aggregation structure changes both the median output and
how many inputs register as influential. At this sample size, however, most
facility inputs (10 to 23 per facility) cannot be told apart from the dummy.
This is the clearest cost of the 250-iteration cap.

# 8. Cross-group patterns

```{r spearman}
sp <- A$spearman[A$spearman$p_adj_BH < 0.05, ]
knitr::kable(sp[order(-abs(sp$rho)), ][1:10, ], digits = 3,
             caption = "Strongest Spearman correlations: curve features vs. mean Tᵢ (BH-adjusted p < 0.05)")
```
